summary: James Smith Reid was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1865 to 1869. He held posts at Christ's College (1869–1880), Pembroke College (1873–1885), and Gonville and Caius College (1878–1926).

James Sutherland Cotton worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Brighton, Winchester, and Trinity College, Oxford (1867–1870), later serving as a fellow and lecturer at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and holding a post at Queens' College, Cambridge (1871–1874).

James Tod worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1798–1799) and under Gyanchandra, later serving in the East India Company (~1799–1823) and as Librarian for the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1835).

James W. Benson is an Indologist who taught James McHugh and Susan J. Rosenfield. He served as Assistant Professor in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and held a post at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

James W. Heisig works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned degrees from Divine Word College, Loyola University Chicago, Notre Dame, and Cambridge (PhD, ~1969–1973), and held long-term posts at Nanzan University and the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (~1978–2010).

James Ward was a philosopher who studied at Mostyn House School, Fitzwilliam College, and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1872–1875). He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1897 to 1925.
James Whitehill worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He founded the Columbia Zen Center and served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000).

James Wilson Bright was a linguist who earned his undergraduate degree at Lafayette College (~1873–1877) and his PhD at Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882). He taught at Cornell (~1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins (1905–1925).

Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Tekchok Dorje, Gyurme Thutop Namgyal, Tai Situ Pema Nyinje Wangpo, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, the latter of whom he also taught.

Jamie Hubbard is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD) under Kazuo Okabe and Minoru Kiyota. He held named professorships in Buddhist, Religion, and East Asian Studies at Smith College (attested 2016, 2026).

Jampa Lhundup is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, where he is attested as a faculty member and Assistant Professor of Art History in 2026.

Jampa Losang Panglung was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Geshe Lharampa at Sera Monastery and degrees from the University of Munich. From circa 1978 to 2004, he was a researcher at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Rinpoche.

Jampa Samten is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as Director (attested 2015) and later as a re-employed Professor (attested 2026).

Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Kalu Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and Tsennyi Tulku Jampal Norbu, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama and 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Dzongsar Khyentse Jamyang Chokyi Wangpo, studied under numerous teachers including Khenpo Thupten and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught figures such as Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Sogyal Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Rigdzin Zangpo and Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé (whom he also taught), and instructed students such as Jamgön Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Jan Baudouin de Courtenay was a linguist who studied under August Leskien and at Warsaw, Berlin, Leipzig, and Charles University. He held posts at Kazan, the Imperial University of Dorpat (1883–1893), Jagiellonian University, Saint Petersburg State University, and the University of Warsaw.

Jan Chozen Bays is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner who studied at Swarthmore, UC San Diego, and under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada. She founded Heart of Wisdom Zen Temple and served as abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery.
